rationale: Position A offers no argued defence and establishes nothing. Position B's mechanics are verified against the reconstruction's record of the pattern: with arm 1 requiring a mandatory `.ya?ml` suffix and arm 2's lookahead `(?![\w.\-/])` rejecting every `.`, `-`, `/`, and word char after `config`, the spellings `cat .faff/config.local` and `cat .faff/config-dev` (extensionless variants) match neither arm — a mechanically checkable false negative. The reconstruction's governing invariant is spelling-completeness for the hand-read floor ('catch the whole class of config-hand-read spellings a skill could use'; 'no unrecognised spelling becomes a silent bypass of the floor'), and the spec's own top principle is 'Cover the whole variant class, not a fixed list.' The two disjoint arms re-impose a de-facto fixed shape (suffix required unless the bare canonical name), which is exactly the narrowing the spec's anti-pattern section condemns. The project's own `.faffrc` precedent — guarded for 'both its canonical name and extensionless form' — confirms extensionless forms are guardable spellings, so the extensionless form of the overlay (`config.local`) and of hyphen-joined variants fall in the same class. The case table and the mandated unit test omit every extensionless-variant row, so the DONE item 'cover the whole variant class' is asserted by prose but contradicted by the pattern, and the spec's own verification apparatus cannot detect the gap. The counterarguments (the actual overlay file is `.faff/config.local.yaml`, so `cat .faff/config.local` reads nothing; the precision rows such as `.faff/config.json` are also non-YAML) are real but do not defeat the defect: the guard is a spelling-shaped tripwire whose regulating principle is completeness without silent bypass, and the spec already flags the extensionless form of the canonical name, making the symmetric extensionless-variant class a genuine, concrete gap rather than a taste call. Because this is a security-floor completeness matter settled by the existing completeness principle and the `.faffrc` precedent (not a product/policy question), and because the proposition is blocking, the fail-safe default applies: UPHOLD_REVIEW.

correction.summary: Widen the `.faff/` arm of the HANDREAD pattern so that dot-separated and hyphen-joined variant spellings without the `.yaml`/`.yml` suffix (e.g. `cat .faff/config.local`, `cat .faff/config-dev`) are also flagged, not merely the suffix-bearing variants plus the bare `cat .faff/config`. Add the extensionless-variant cases as flag rows in the §3 case table and assert them in the mandated unit test, so the verified class includes every dot-/hyphen-delimited variant spelling regardless of suffix; keep all existing negative rows (`.faff/config.json`, `.faff/config-notes.md`, `.faff/config/extra.yaml`, `.faff/configuration.yaml`), the verb-gating, the `.faffrc` branch, and the `.example` carve-out unchanged.

rationale: Position A's factual premises hold — the §3 case table indeed contains no `.example` row, and the DONE item "A `.faff/config.example.yaml` line is NOT flagged" exists in §8 — but its inference does not. The reconstruction establishes that the governing precedent `born-verifiable-done-means-decidable-not-one-dedicated-scenario-per-done-item` accepts a test *or an observation* as a decider, provided the spec names what would be run and the pass condition. The `.example` DONE item is carried by a named code-inspection confirmation, not by a table row: §7's assumption explicitly names the observation (confirm the `if (line.includes(".example")) continue;` line still precedes the `HANDREAD` match in `validate-adapters.js`) and the pass condition (the line-skip precedes the match). The spec also deliberately keeps the carve-out out of the pattern's case table — §1 states the widened pattern "is not relied on to exempt" `.example` lines, and §4's edge case restates the mechanism. Position A's predicted consequence — that the build can pass while the line-skip is dropped or reordered and the DONE item is "checked off without any test deciding it" — is not concrete and checkable against the requirements: the DONE item is decided by the named observation, which the precedent accepts, and scenario 5 additionally covers the `.example` line behaviour. The objection that a decidable DONE item lacks a 1:1 test pin is precisely the taste-level objection the precedent excludes from defect status. Position B offers no counter-argument, but Position A has not established a material defect on the merits.
